question: How does Athelney Jones's confidence in his own handling of the Norwood case change as The Sign of the Four goes on?
verified:
At Pondicherry Lodge Jones is brusque and sure of himself: he dismisses theories, announces that Thaddeus Sholto killed his brother and walked off with the treasure, and arrests Thaddeus, the gatekeeper, the housekeeper and the Indian servant. Later his theory collapses because Thaddeus proves an unshakable alibi, and he comes to Baker Street downcast, meek and apologetic, admitting his professional credit is at stake and asking for help, and praising Holmes. Once the launch has caught Small he again gives himself airs, and at the end he is angry when the treasure box is found empty.

Evidence (verbatim):
- [0ee225a9a3b5fbc2:9:8] "Sholto was, on his own confession, with his brother last night."
- [0ee225a9a3b5fbc2:9:10] "“Facts are better than mere theories, after all."
- [0ee225a9a3b5fbc2:10:4] "He has arrested not only friend Thaddeus, but the gatekeeper, the housekeeper, and the Indian servant."
- [0ee225a9a3b5fbc2:12:8] "Very different was he, however, from the brusque and masterful professor of common sense who had taken over the case so confidently at Upper Norwood."
- [0ee225a9a3b5fbc2:12:8] "His expression was downcast, and his bearing meek and even apologetic."
- [0ee225a9a3b5fbc2:12:9] "He was able to prove an alibi which could not be shaken."
- [0ee225a9a3b5fbc2:12:9] "It’s a very dark case, and my professional credit is at stake. I should be very glad of a little assistance."
- [0ee225a9a3b5fbc2:12:9] "I never saw the case yet that he could not throw a light upon."
- [0ee225a9a3b5fbc2:14:4] "It was amusing to notice how the consequential Jones was already beginning to give himself airs on the strength of the capture."

question: Which characters in The Sign of the Four keep faith with the people they swore to stand by, and which ones break it?
verified:
Jonathan Small and his three Sikh comrades swear that each will always act for all, and Small says he has never broken that oath. He holds to it when the officers want only him and he answers 'None or all', and Captain Morstan remarks that Small is a man of his word who does not flinch from his friend. Major Sholto, by contrast, goes to India to test the story but never comes back, and Morstan finds the treasure stolen, without any of the conditions of the bargain carried out. At the end Small throws the treasure into the Thames rather than let Sholto's or Morstan's kin have it, saying he has acted all through for his three comrades as much as himself.

Evidence (verbatim):
- [0ee225a9a3b5fbc2:15:24] "we had sworn that we should each always act for all, so that none might take advantage. That is an oath that I can put my hand to my heart and swear that I have never broken."
- [0ee225a9a3b5fbc2:15:32] "‘None or all,’ I answered. ‘We have sworn it. The four of us must always act together.’"
- [0ee225a9a3b5fbc2:15:32] "‘You see, Morstan,’ said he, ‘Small is a man of his word. He does not flinch from his friend."
- [0ee225a9a3b5fbc2:15:33] "The villain Sholto went off to India, but he never came back again."
- [0ee225a9a3b5fbc2:15:34] "The scoundrel had stolen it all, without carrying out one of the conditions on which we had sold him the secret."
- [0ee225a9a3b5fbc2:15:1] "I have acted all through for them as much as for myself. It’s been the sign of four with us always."
- [0ee225a9a3b5fbc2:15:1] "throw the treasure into the Thames rather than let it go to kith or kin of Sholto or of Morstan"

question: How did Jefferson Hope and Lucy Ferrier first meet, and where did things stand between them when he left for the mountains?
verified:
Hope, a hunter returning from prospecting in the Nevada mountains, caught Lucy's frightened horse when she was caught in a drove of cattle. He asked her to tell her father to remember the Jefferson Hopes of St. Louis, since his father and Ferrier had been close, and she invited him to call. He then visited the farm many times and became a favourite with the old farmer, while Lucy's blushes showed her heart was no longer her own. When he set off again he asked whether she would be ready to come when he returned in a couple of months, and told her that Ferrier had given his consent provided the mines worked out.

- [05ab674df048d13f:13:7] "When you see him, ask him if he remembers the Jefferson Hopes of St. Louis. If he’s the same Ferrier, my father and he were pretty thick."
- [05ab674df048d13f:13:8] "He and they had been among the Nevada Mountains prospecting for silver"
- [05ab674df048d13f:13:9] "He called on John Ferrier that night, and many times again, until his face was a familiar one at the farm-house."

question: What did Mrs. Charpentier tell Gregson about how Enoch Drebber behaved while he lodged with her, and what happened on the evening he left?
verified:
Drebber, who had boarded with her for nearly three weeks with his secretary Stangerson, was coarse and brutish, drunk from the day he arrived and free and familiar with the maids. He pressed his attentions on her daughter Alice, once seizing her in his arms, which made even Stangerson reproach him. She gave him notice and he drove off, but within the hour he returned drunk, said he had missed his train, proposed that Alice run away with him and caught her by the wrist. Her son Arthur came in, there was a scuffle, and Arthur went after him with a stick, returning after she had gone to bed.

Evidence (verbatim):
- [05ab674df048d13f:10:8] "He was coarse in his habits and brutish in his ways."
- [05ab674df048d13f:10:8] "On one occasion he actually seized her in his arms and embraced her—an outrage which caused his own secretary to reproach him for his unmanly conduct."
- [05ab674df048d13f:10:9] "I gave him notice to leave on account of it."
- [05ab674df048d13f:10:9] "He then turned to Alice, and before my very face, proposed to her that she should fly with him."
- [05ab674df048d13f:10:9] "but he caught her by the wrist and endeavoured to draw her towards the door."
- [05ab674df048d13f:10:10] "I saw Arthur standing in the doorway laughing, with a stick in his hand."
- [05ab674df048d13f:10:10] "“I don’t think that fine fellow will trouble us again,” he said. “I will just go after him and see what he does with himself.”"

question: How does Holmes's state of mind change from the opening of The Sign of the Four to its last page?
verified:
The book opens with Holmes idle and on cocaine, saying he cannot live without brain-work. Once Thaddeus Sholto's case takes hold he is restless, pacing the rooms and snapping at Mrs. Hudson, then on the night of the chase he is in nervous exaltation, brilliant and gay after his black depression. When it is over he says the reaction has come and he will be limp for a week, admits there are in him the makings of a fine loafer and a spry fellow, and when Watson asks what remains for him, reaches for the cocaine bottle.

- [0ee225a9a3b5fbc2:12:2] "After you was gone he walked and he walked, up and down, and up and down, until I was weary of the sound of his footstep."
- [0ee225a9a3b5fbc2:13:0] "He appeared to be in a state of nervous exaltation. I have never known him so brilliant."
- [0ee225a9a3b5fbc2:13:0] "His bright humour marked the reaction from his black depression of the preceding days."

- [0ee225a9a3b5fbc2:15:43] "And he stretched his long white hand up for it."

question: How do Watson's feelings for Mary Morstan show themselves as The Sign of the Four goes on?
verified:
At first sight Watson judges her face the clearest promise of a refined and sensitive nature he has ever seen. Waiting in the dark outside Pondicherry Lodge, her hand is in his, and he notes that their hands sought each other without any word of affection. When he carries the empty treasure box to her he speaks jovially though his heart is heavy. Once the treasure is gone he says 'Thank God', takes her hand, which she does not withdraw, and tells her he loves her because the riches had sealed his lips, and she answers 'Thank God' too.

Evidence (verbatim):
- [0ee225a9a3b5fbc2:5:0] "I have never looked upon a face which gave a clearer promise of a refined and sensitive nature."
- [0ee225a9a3b5fbc2:8:3] "Miss Morstan and I stood together, and her hand was in mine."
- [0ee225a9a3b5fbc2:8:3] "in an hour of trouble our hands instinctively sought for each other."
- [0ee225a9a3b5fbc2:14:6] "speaking jovially and boisterously, though my heart was heavy within me."
- [0ee225a9a3b5fbc2:14:9] "“Because you are within my reach again,” I said, taking her hand. She did not withdraw it."
- [0ee225a9a3b5fbc2:14:9] "Now that they are gone I can tell you how I love you."

question: Two servants in the Sholto household turn out to matter in The Sign of the Four. How does each one act toward his master's secrets?
verified:
Lal Chowdar was Major Sholto's faithful old servant. He let Morstan in on the night he died, overheard the quarrel and the blow, said his lips were sealed, and helped the Major hide the body; he knew where the treasure was hidden and has since died. Lal Rao is the butler of Bartholomew's household, whom Mrs. Bernstone distrusted, and Holmes suspects of being inside contact for Small; at the end Holmes says he was the confederate in the house.

- [0ee225a9a3b5fbc2:7:9] "Lal Chowdar and I disposed of the body that night"

question: Jonathan Small and Jefferson Hope are both caught and both talk. How does each defend himself, and which killings does each own up to?
verified:
Hope owns the killings openly and treats them as justice: he says he decided to be judge, jury and executioner, claims he is as much an officer of justice as the detectives, and says he did not mean to kill Drebber in cold blood but offered him the poisoned-pill choice. Small disowns the death of Bartholomew Sholto, swearing he never raised a hand against him and blaming Tonga, with whom he says he had no quarrel; he says he would gladly have killed the old Major. About Achmet's murder he does not deny it but argues it was his life or the merchant's, and that few would have refused a share of the loot.

Evidence (verbatim):
- [05ab674df048d13f:17:3] "I determined that I should be judge, jury, and executioner all rolled into one."
- [05ab674df048d13f:17:10] "“Don’t imagine that I intended to kill him in cold blood."
- [05ab674df048d13f:17:16] "You may consider me to be a murderer; but I hold that I am just as much an officer of justice as you are."
- [0ee225a9a3b5fbc2:14:0] "I give you my word on the book that I never raised hand against Mr. Sholto. It was that little hell-hound Tonga who shot one of his cursed darts into him."
- [0ee225a9a3b5fbc2:14:1] "Now, if it had been the old major I would have swung for him with a light heart."
- [0ee225a9a3b5fbc2:14:1] "But it’s cursed hard that I should be lagged over this young Sholto, with whom I had no quarrel whatever."
- [0ee225a9a3b5fbc2:15:22] "Besides, it was my life or his when once he was in the fort."
- [0ee225a9a3b5fbc2:15:22] "I should like to know how many fellows in my shoes would have refused a share of this loot"

question: How did the relationship between Joseph Stangerson and Enoch Drebber change between Utah and London?
verified:
In Utah they were rivals for Lucy Ferrier: there were words between them as to which should have her, Stangerson having shot her father, but Drebber's party was stronger in council and the Prophet gave her to him. Later both left the Church, and Drebber turned much of his property into money and went off wealthy while Stangerson was comparatively poor. In Cleveland Stangerson had become Drebber's private secretary, and in London he is a quiet, reserved man in his employer's service, who reproaches Drebber's unmanly conduct toward Alice Charpentier.

question: How do Gregson and Lestrade's attitudes toward the Drebber case change between the morning Gregson announces an arrest and the day the murderer is finally taken?
verified:

He is crestfallen to find Holmes already noticed the hat and triumphant over Lestrade's confusion. When Lestrade brings news of Stangerson's murder Gregson jumps up, upsets his drink and stammers; the two of them then admit they have both failed and press Holmes to say what he knows. question: What did Jefferson Hope do in Utah after he found out what had happened to the Ferriers, and why did he go back to the mines?
verified:
Finding Ferrier's grave and learning that Lucy had been taken, Hope resolved to devote his life to revenge. On the night before her burial he walked into the room where the other wives sat with her body, kissed her forehead and took the wedding-ring from her finger, saying she should not be buried in it. For some months he stayed in the mountains and attacked the two young Mormons: a bullet through Stangerson's window and a boulder dropped at Drebber. When they took precautions he returned to the Nevada mines to recover his health and earn money to pursue them, staying nearly five years.

Evidence (verbatim):
- [05ab674df048d13f:16:6] "If there was nothing else left to him, he could at least devote his life to revenge."
- [05ab674df048d13f:16:10] "Stooping over her, he pressed his lips reverently to her cold forehead, and then, snatching up her hand, he took the wedding-ring from her finger."
- [05ab674df048d13f:16:10] "“She shall not be buried in that,” he cried with a fierce snarl"
- [05ab674df048d13f:16:11] "Once a bullet whistled through Stangerson’s window and flattened itself upon the wall within a foot of him."
- [05ab674df048d13f:16:11] "On another occasion, as Drebber passed under a cliff a great boulder crashed down on him"

question: The Sholto brothers did not see eye to eye about Mary Morstan. How did each regard what was owed to her, and what did the quarrel lead one of them to do?
verified:
Thaddeus held that they were her trustees and that it would be bad taste to treat a young lady so scurvily; he wanted her to have her due and says he will do her justice whatever Bartholomew says. Bartholomew was averse to part with the pearls, being, in Thaddeus's words, inclined to the Major's fault, and could not see it that way. Thaddeus had to persuade him to let him send her a pearl at intervals so she would never feel destitute. Their difference went so far that Thaddeus left Pondicherry Lodge and set up rooms of his own, and when the treasure was found he told Mary and Bartholomew angrily objected.

- [0ee225a9a3b5fbc2:7:13] "It was all that I could do to persuade him to let me find out Miss Morstan’s address and send her a detached pearl at fixed intervals, so that at least she might never feel destitute."

- [0ee225a9a3b5fbc2:7:14] "Our difference of opinion on this subject went so far that I thought it best to set up rooms for myself: so I left Pondicherry Lodge"

- [0ee225a9a3b5fbc2:7:5] "He is very angry with me for taking the course which has seemed right to me."

question: What does Watson notice about Holmes's vanity in each of the two novels, and what does Holmes do that shows it?
verified:
In A Study in Scarlet, when Watson compares him to Poe's Dupin, Holmes says Dupin was a very inferior fellow, and later when Watson praises his detection as an exact science he flushes with pleasure, and Watson notes he is as sensitive to flattery about his art as any girl about her beauty. In The Sign of the Four Holmes calls himself the last and highest court of appeal in detection, and Watson is irritated by the egotism that seemed to demand that every line of his pamphlet be devoted to Holmes's own doings.

question: In both novels the killer had a helper. How does each killer treat that helper when he is questioned, and what does it show about his loyalty?
verified:
Hope will not give up his accomplice: asked who came for the ring, he says he can tell his own secrets but does not get other people into trouble, and boasts the friend did it smartly. Small, in contrast, immediately blames Tonga for the dart that killed Bartholomew and says he would have half killed him for leaving the club behind, yet later calls him stanch and true and says no man ever had a more faithful mate. So Hope protects his ally by silence while Small's loyalty to Tonga is real but he is ready to put the blame on him.

- [05ab674df048d13f:17:17] "I think you’ll own he did it smartly."

question: As The Sign of the Four goes on, what does Holmes ask Watson to do on his own, and what does it say about how he regards him?
verified:
At Pondicherry Lodge Holmes tells Watson that his presence will be of great service and has him feel the dead man's arm and say what killed him, then sends him off, after escorting Miss Morstan, to fetch Toby from the bird-stuffer. Later Holmes leaves him at Baker Street as his representative, to open all notes and telegrams and act on his own judgment, asking if he can rely on him.

question: In each novel a daughter's fate follows from what happened to her father. What does each father do for his daughter, and how does each daughter show her attachment to him?
verified:
John Ferrier gave up his ruined farm for Lucy's honour and happiness, comforted her when the Prophet threatened them ('We'll fix it up somehow') and sent for Hope to help. Lucy, in turn, says it is for her father that she is frightened, holds him back by the arm when he would rush for his gun, and after his death never holds her head up and dies within a month. Captain Morstan's telegram to Mary is full of kindness and love, and he vanishes soon after; Mary says she knew in her heart that he was dead and years later, her care is shown by how she preserved the Agra plan from all her father's papers.
